doc.title: Pete Jolly interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 15, 1999

title: Pay with Rodgers and the Festival of Modern American Jazz tour
summary: He earned $175 a week with Rodgers' quintet on a long package tour with Kenton, Art Tatum and Charlie Ventura.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: What kind of money was he offering back then for that kind of gig?
Oh God. Okay when I went on the road with Shorty Rodgers I got $175 a week.
That’s probably a lot more than some people were making though, huh?

Well to me it was great you know. Of course what was great was playing with these guys, playing with Shelly and that kind of a rhythm section, Curtis Counce was in the rhythm section, Curtis played bass. And Jimmy Giuffre. That was the band, and Shorty, it was a quintet. And it was a long tour. It started in San Diego and we might have even played in Syracuse, I don’t — it was called The Festival of Modern American Jazz, 195 — end of ’54. And it was Stan Kenton’s orchestra, Art Tatum trio, Charlie Ventura with MaryAnn McCall, and a piano player from Massachusetts was playing with her. He plays solo all the time, you know who I mean.
Dave. Yeah. Dave was playing piano with Charlie Ventura. Then they had Jimmy Smith and he did a thing. It was like two busloads.
Oh yeah, it was great. Every night.
